{{Short description|American cell biologist}}

'''Vincent Joseph Cristofalo''' (1933{{mdash}}2006) was an American cell biologist.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Journals of Gerontology |url=https://academic.oup.com/biomedgerontology/article/61/7/639/822607 |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=academic.oup.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Vincent Cristofalo (1933-2006): Extraordinary Gerontologist |date=2006 |doi=10.1007/BF03324845 |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF03324845.pdf |access-date=2024-02-06 |last1=Adelman |first1=Richard |last2=Hayflick |first2=Leonard |last3=Masoro |first3=Edward |last4=Sell |first4=Christian |journal=Aging Clinical and Experimental Research |volume=18 |issue=6 |pages=463–469 |pmid=17366698 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Philadelphia]], Cristofalo received his [[undergraduate degree]] from St. Joseph's College and a [[master's degree]] from [[Temple University]], followed by a [[PhD]] in [[physiology]] and [[biochemistry]] from the [[University of Delaware]] in 1962.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/05/18/us/18cristofalo.html|title=Vincent Cristofalo, 73, Expert on the Aging of Human Cells, Is Dead|first=Jeremy|last=Pearce|date=May 18, 2006|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://almanac.upenn.edu/archive/volumes/v52/n34/obit.html|title=05/23/06, Deaths - Almanac, Vol. 52, No. 34|website=almanac.upenn.edu}}</ref>

In 1967, Cristofalo joined the [[University of Pennsylvania]] as an [[assistant professor]] of [[animal biology]] and contributed to the establishment of the Institute on Aging.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1"/> His academic tenure included appointments in [[physiology]] and social work.<ref name="auto"/> Additionally, he held positions at various institutions, including the [[Lankenau Institute for Medical Research]], where he served as president, and faculties at Temple University, the [[Wistar Institute]], the Medical College of Pennsylvania, [[Allegheny University of the Health Sciences]], and [[Thomas Jefferson University]].<ref name="auto"/>

In his administrative roles, Cristofalo was president of the [[Gerontological Society of America]] in 1990 and the [[American Federation for Aging Research]] from 1996 to 1998.<ref name="auto"/> He also served as an editor for the ''[[Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences]]''.<ref name="auto"/>

==Research==
Cristofalo's early research focused on [[cancer cell]] [[metabolism]] before shifting to the study of the lifespan of healthy cells and cell senescence.<ref name="auto"/> His research explored the effects of factors such as [[oxygen]], [[vitamin E]], and [[hydrocortisone]] on [[cell replication]], and he investigated aging and cellular degeneration from a genetic and evolutionary perspective.<ref name="auto"/>

Cristofalo co-authored a paper in 1998, titled "Relationship Between Donor Age and the Replicative Life Span of Human Cells in Culture," published in The ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]''.<ref name="auto"/> The study presented data challenging the then-prevailing belief about the reduced replicative capacity of cells from older individuals.<ref name="auto"/>
